entries.text: Merging a save into the starter roster you haven't arranged yet now lays the whole board out fresh, with couples side by side and children under their parents, just as Replace does.

When the board lays out your save, couples sit side by side, children sit right under their parents, and households line up with their family next door. Boards you have arranged keep every card where it is.
Fixed: sims you gave they/them or other pronouns in Create a Sim are Non-Binary on the board again, after a save import made them Female or Male. Their pronouns show in the sim editor.
Undo and Redo now say the whole step, never cut short with …, and names of sims, households and worlds stand out in their own colour there and on the status line.
Your arrangement holds: any edit, whatever it is, now leaves every card it isn't about exactly where it is. Only Organise, loading a file, importing a save and Undo/Redo rearrange the board.
Fixed: planning a marriage or another link no longer shifts the worlds around the couple; every card stays where it is.
Redo (Ctrl/⌘ Shift Z) puts back what Undo took back; its tip names the step, and on a phone it waits at the top of More.
The Undo button's tip names the change it will take back ("Undo: Add a sim to Gooseman"), and after an undo the status line says what was undone.

Planned sims with no name are numbered only when two or more share a last name, and the numbers are recounted on every change, so there are no gaps. A couple's new baby asks which last name it takes when the parents' differ.

Adding a sim, moving in with a partner, a planned baby or joining a household no longer pushes other households or worlds: the household grows into free room, or moves whole to free room in its world when it has none, and the status line says so.
Moving a household to another world no longer shoves other worlds around: it lands in free room in its new world, where that world is on your board, and every other card stays put.

Plan heirs generations ahead: pick "Heir after Eric" for his daughter, and "Heir after Olivia" for hers. The Family tab shows the line of succession, cards say "Lewis heir after Eric", and a save that makes Eric head makes Olivia the planned heir. Boards with an heir planned at each generation turn into a line.
Highlight leaves out the deceased: they never light up, and the counts are of living sims only. The widowed count as Single, and a child who died no longer counts for No children.
A couple's + can adopt too: pick someone younger than both, and both become their parents. A child with birth and adoptive parents hangs from each couple's badge.

The + on a card now asks: a new sim, or adopt one. Adopt lists the sims who could be: younger and not family yet. Connect can plan an adoption, a divorce or a breakup, and says which links two sims have already.
Merging a save no longer drops a wedding you planned for an engaged couple, and an engaged couple your game has married now shows as married.
Adopted children say so. Their link reads Parent → child (adopted), and the Log says who adopted whom. Merge your save into your board to mark them; nothing moves.
Little arrowheads show which way each link runs: into a child's card, out of a couple's pill, where a line branches off, and into each partner. They're gray, or violet when planned.

Lines go round sim cards now. Parent lines take a clear way down instead of cutting through the cards in their path, and marriage and romance lines between far-apart sims go under or round the cards between them.
A line from a parent to a child beside them no longer runs through the parent and joins the grandparent's line.

Plans can tell a story now. Moving a sim somewhere and back keeps both moves as steps, and the bin in the Log takes out just one step. Couples can have a planned divorce or breakup: select the link and choose Plan a divorce or Plan a breakup, or press Delete on a couple from your save. The line turns violet with a divorce mark or a struck heart, the Log and household plan list it, and a save that shows them apart marks it done.

Plans can be cancelled. Each line in the Log's Plan tab has a bin that puts the board back as your game has it: a planned link goes, a planned baby goes with its links, and a move sends its sims (or a whole household) back where they live in your game. Moving a sim back by hand cancels its move too, and a sim moved twice shows as one move from where they are in your game. Undo brings any of it back.

The sim editor's move buttons now read Move sim to another household and Move household to another world, with sim and household in bold so the two are easy to tell apart. Long labels wrap inside the button instead of running out of it.
Highlight has a Not born yet chip at the start of Life stage, for the planned babies whose cards say Not born yet. It adds up with the ages you pick, so Not born yet and Infant shows both.

The ♥ menu now lists partners in the same cards as Possible partners in the sim editor: the dynasty role's mark, how close in age and their household, then in amber whether they're related, married or in a romance, not aging now, and their dynasty.

A household can now move to another world whole: open its plan from its tag, or a sim's editor, and choose Move to another world. It keeps its name and everyone in it, and joins a household of that name if the world has one. The Log and the plan show it as one move, like "The Dreamer household moves from Not in any world to Ondarion". Moving one sim into a new household named like their own, in another world, now offers to move the whole household instead. Moves between worlds name both worlds, so they no longer read "from Dreamer to Dreamer".

Highlight has two new rows. Family adds No children, beside Single, for sims with no child on the board, planned babies counted. Dynasty picks heads, heirs, members with no role, and outcasts. Picks in one row add up, while different rows narrow each other, so Young Adult, Female, Single, No children and Member finds single female young adults with no children who are plain members of a dynasty.

Hover or select a sim and a ♥ shows on each side of the card: it plans a partner. Pick married, romance, secret lovers or divorced, then type a name or click them on the board. Picked by name for a marriage or romance, the board asks whether one moves in with the other, and puts their card beside their partner's.
Selecting a family's line now shows every child on its chip, over as many lines as it takes, instead of cutting the last ones off. The chip also counts them: "Parents → 3 children".

Your plan notes now show beyond the Log: under each plan in a household's brief, on a selected link, and in the save review when the game went against a plan, so the reason is there when you decide to keep it or follow the game.

The Log now has two tabs: Plan, for links and moves still to do, with anything off plan on top, and In your game, for what your saves show and the plans they showed done (marked ✓ planned). Lines are quieter: no pill on each, just the time, and places in the names' tooltips. You can add a note to any link or move, like why you're pairing two sims, and it stays with the plan when a save shows it done.

Dynasties with no heir, or with 2 sims or fewer to carry them on, now say they are at risk: in the Dynasties panel, with why, and on their members’ cards. The panel can also sort by size (Most sims, Fewest sims) and show only the dynasties at risk.

Up next says what playing a household does: “Helps the Le Chien household: Planned (2) Romeo is born here”. A planned baby now waits on its parents’ household, a sim moved on the board grows up where the game still has them, and a household that isn’t in your game yet comes last, saying who has to move in first.

The Worlds card now starts with your board's totals: how many worlds have sims and how many households there are. The household total includes those not in any world, so it adds up to the world tags, and a note under each total says how many worlds filters hide and how many households are in no world.
World tags now count dynasties too: a crown and the number of dynasties with a living sim in that world, after its sims and households. Hover a tag to see how many of them are only planned.

Two dynasties can now share a name. When you create a dynasty with a name another one already has, the Dynasty menu warns you and offers to join the existing one instead. If you keep both, each one shows its founder, like "Scott (Travis’s line)" and "Scott (Sara’s line)", in the menu, the Dynasties panel, on cards and in plan steps.

The premades' unknown fathers (Hauata, Behr, Elderberry, Nishidake, Hoffman, Perry, Pleasant) are now deceased, on the roster and when a save is loaded, and Kaori's and Lia's grandparents show as grandparents. Bring one back by setting their state by hand: later save uploads leave it as you set it.

Rohan Elderberry's unknown father is now deceased, on the starter roster and whenever a save is loaded, and the roster shows Ekram and Eleanor as Rohan's grandparents, as the game does. Upload your save again to update a board that already has him.

In the Dynasties panel, the highlighter beside a dynasty keeps its members lit on the board until you press Done or Esc. Its banner says how many households and worlds they span, and Show all fits them all on screen.
A sim's card now names their dynasty on its last line, like "Resident · Capp dynasty": faded while only planned, crossed out while planned to leave, and nothing for a sim in no dynasty.
In the Dynasties panel, open a planned dynasty to Rename it or Remove it. Remove asks first and takes the dynasty off all its members, leaving their cards, and Undo brings it back.

A Dynasties button (the crown, beside Up next) lists every dynasty, in your game and planned, with how many sims each has, its head and heir. Hover one to light up its members on the board, wherever they live; open it to see who they are and click one to go to them. Search by dynasty or by a sim's name. On a phone, Up next and Dynasties are in the More menu, and the top bar no longer runs off the edge at some window widths.

A planned dynasty can be renamed: pick it in a member's Family tab and click Rename beside Dynasty. The new name goes on all its members' cards at once, and Undo takes it back. A name another dynasty already has is refused, and dynasties from your game keep the name your save gives them.

A plan to start a dynasty with a teen as its head now waits until they are a young adult, as the game requires, instead of showing as ready. It says how long they have left, and a planned baby as head waits to be born and grow up.
The sim editor's ✕ no longer sits on the last name field: it has a space of its own beside the name fields, and is a little bigger to hit.

A sim's card has a + on its bottom edge, as a couple has under its ring: click it to plan a baby of that sim alone, in their household with their last name. It shows when you hover over or select the card. Link a second parent later with Connect if there is one.

The Dynasty menu has a search box at its top. Your sim's family's dynasties come first, their parents' leading, each with who links them ("Dirk Dreamer, father"); the rest are split into In your game and Planned, with how many sims each has. Type a name no dynasty has to create it. Possible partners have a Find by name box too, and sims the same distance in age are now listed A to Z instead of looking shuffled.
The Dynasty menu now starts with "➕ Create a new dynasty…", the way "➕ Create a new household…" starts the household menu.

Every sim now has a generation, dynasty or not, counted from their oldest known ancestor on the board ("Gen 4 from Queen Thebe"). In the editor, pick a sim's dynasty first, then their role, which can be "Member, no role". You can start a dynasty your game doesn't have yet with "New dynasty…", and a planned baby is suggested its family's dynasty. Joining, leaving or changing role stays part of your plan until a save shows it.

An unnamed planned baby's card now says whose child it is, like "Child of Jules ＋ Bess", so planned siblings and cousins with the same last name tell apart at a glance. Hover it for the parents' full names.

Planned sims with no first name are numbered by last name, "Planned (1) Le Chien", "Planned (2) Le Chien", on cards, in the log and in plans, and keep their number when another is named or born. A sim can't be saved without a last name: the field turns red and Save waits. Household moves are now part of each household's plan, and turn done in the log once your save has the sim living there.

A dynasty role you set is now part of your plan, like a link you drew. For a sim your save has in no dynasty, the editor asks which dynasty they'll join (their parents' by default), so a planned heir gets a generation too. The role's mark shows faded until a save has it, save imports keep it meanwhile, and the household's plan lists it, like "Make Heir Dreamer heir of the Dreamer dynasty". Whoever holds the role in your save keeps it until your game changes.
Dragging is now undoable: after moving a card, a selection, a household or a whole world, ⌘Z (or Undo) puts it back where it was.

Up next, the numbered-list button in the top bar, suggests an order to play your households in when you'd like a plan to follow. Plays that move other households' plans come first, then an elder short on days, the most ready, the oldest generation, and whoever you played longest ago, each with why. Open plan takes you there; Skip for now puts a household last until your next save import.

Household tags now carry a plan badge beside Age up and +: "2 ready" in green when something can be done today, "1 off plan" in amber when the game went another way, or "waiting" when everything waits on someone. Households with nothing pending stay quiet. Click the badge to open the household's plan.

Click a household's name tag to see its plan: what's ready to do now, what's waiting and on whom (with a countdown and which household to play), what the game did instead, how long each elder has, and what playing it moves along for other households. Hover a line to light its sims up on the board. It also opens from a sim's editor ("See the Munch household's plan"); drag the tag as before to move the household.

Groundwork for household briefs: the board now works out each household's plan. A planned couple or baby is ready when everyone is grown up, waiting when someone is too young or not born yet (and says which household to play to move it), and off plan when the game went another way.

A sim's age details now count down to Young Adult, not only to the next stage: a child on Short is a Young Adult in 17 days of aging. Elders say how long they've been one and when old age can come at the earliest, like "Elder for 2.4 days · old age in 4+ days". It's the earliest, never a date: traits like Long Lived stretch it, and your save doesn't say by how much.

The board is cool white and blue-gray instead of beige: the top bar, panels, chips, borders and the board itself. Colors that mean something keep theirs: blue buttons, amber warnings, the yellow search match, the gold highlight, violet plans and each world's color.

A planned baby's last name follows its household, not the parent you clicked first: the household's own name when a parent has it, else the parent's name more of the household shares, never a roommate's. When the parents tie, like a Sterling and a Rico in a new household, the couple's + asks which last name, as the game does at a birth. When the parents live apart, each household choice says the last name it brings.

Naming a planned kid no longer swaps it with its sibling: any edit that changes how the board sorts cards, a first name included, now keeps every card where it is. A new planned kid lands beside its siblings on their row, right or left, instead of dropping further down the board when the spot next to them is taken.
A planned sim's Plan label suggests "e.g. Firstborn, Future spouse" instead of one player's own "Heir 1, Spare 1" system. Name your planned sims however you like.

The Your plan step asks about a planned baby inside the plan it depends on. When Beatrice married Adekoya instead of Dirk, Heir Dreamer is asked about right under that choice: follow the game and pick one of the triplets, or keep your plan and wait for a baby with Dirk. Each choice says what happens, and the step opens with its one rule: your save is the truth about names, genders, ages and parents. A planned parent your save overrules is dropped when a real sim fills the planned card, and Unlink plans them again.

Your plan meets your save. Merging a save now has a Your plan step: planned sims the save can fill (a planned child matched by its parents, a planned spouse through their partner), and plans your game went against, like a planned couple where one married someone else. Choose Follow the game, Keep my plan, Drop it or Decide later; off-plan plans show ⚠ on the board and in the editor. A planned sim's editor can link it to a sim from your save by hand, and Unlink undoes it. Planned children start as "Not born yet" with a plan label instead of a made-up name, and the Log counts what is planned, done and off plan.

Possible partners has an Age menu beside Gender, with how many fit each life stage, and a checkbox to hide sims in Not in any world or Unhoused, remembered from sim to sim. Long partner rows wrap, so the sim editor no longer scrolls sideways.

Possible partners keep to age groups: young adults, adults and elders are suggested to each other, teens to teens, children to children, and infants and toddlers together. The list is split by life stage, with the closest three in each and a Show more for the rest.

Family-tree ancestors the game records no death for are marked deceased when their children are elders or have all died, like the Darongs' and the Altos' Unknown great-grandmothers; loading your save again updates cards already on the board. An ancestor shared by two dynasties shows both lines ("Gen 1 of the Darong line, also Gen 1 of the Dreamer line"). The sim editor has separate First name and Last name fields.
Divorces from your save are drawn gray, like marriages. Violet now always means planned on the board and not in your save yet, divorces included.

The legend's Links card is now the Key, grouped into family lines, couples, card marks and your plans, with each mark drawn as the board draws it. Click Key to fold it away once you know the marks; it stays folded. On phones the legend scrolls as one sheet with larger text.

The sim editor has tabs: Sim for life stage, gender, life state, playability and moving house; Family for dynasty role, generation and possible partners; Details for the age facts from your save, where the sim comes from and their sim ID. The name stays at the top and Save at the bottom, so you no longer scroll to reach it. The editor opens on the tab you used last.

Search has room to type again on laptop screens. Your save's lifespan and season length move from the top bar to the status bar at the bottom, beside Autosave, and still open the game time and Auto Age options. Search widens while you type, and on narrower windows the top bar drops labels step by step instead of squeezing the search field.

Dynasty generations count from the first head's oldest known ancestor, deceased sims and family-tree relatives included: Cordelia Thebe V is Gen 5 of the Thebe, under Queen Thebe. The editor says who Gen 1 is, and Count from lets you start the count from someone else on the line.

Deceased sims' cards fade, and Filters → Hide deceased takes them off the board (saved with the board, like Hide secrets). Ages in Filters is now Highlight, grouped into life stage, gender, relationship and pets, and it says how many sims your chips pick out, such as "25 male elders", in the panel and in a banner on the board.

The top bar fits on a phone again. Connect, Add sim, Delete, Undo, Filters, search and More stay in it as full-size buttons; Organise, Log, Family links and boxes, and Your save (the lifespan and season length from your last save) move to the top of the More menu.

Loading a save now reads how your game ages sims. A chip in the bar shows its lifespan and season length, with the game time and Auto Age options behind it. The sim editor shows when a sim was born, how long they have lived, how far into their life stage they are and the days to the next one. Dynasty members show their generation, counted from the dynasty's first head ("Gen 2 of the Goth"), and Possible partners lists unrelated sims closest in life.

Cards mark dynasties: 👑 the head, ⚜️ the heir and 🥀 an outcast, read from a Royalty & Legacy save or set in the editor's new Dynasty role field. Hover over a marked name to see its dynasty. The legend explains the marks.
The chip on a selected link joins names with a plus: Ignacio Robles + Jade Rosa → Heir Rosa.

Move several sims to another household, or a new one, at once: Shift-click them (or click them with Select on), then choose Move to household in the bar that appears. One undo puts them all back. In the editor too, Create a new household now comes first in the list.

Filters can highlight sims by gender: Female, Male or Non-Binary. A gender chip narrows the ages you pick, so Female with Young Adult lights only young adult women, and with a pet chip it picks out female cats, dogs or horses.
A premade who came in under a married name loses the save badge once the board knows them by their own name again.

When the game, or a mod such as MC Command Center, gives a married sim their spouse's surname, the board keeps their own: Cassandra stays Cassandra Goth after marrying Caleb Vatore. The editor shows the married name, Find a sim finds either name, and typing the married name in the editor puts it on the card.
A selected link between households keeps proper dashes at any zoom, instead of turning into a comb of short vertical ticks.
Family links inside a household are strong solid lines; links between households are thin and dashed, so each household's own tree stands out. The legend shows both.
Scrolling zooms the board again, with a mouse wheel or a trackpad; drag an empty spot to move around. The Getting around tips are rewritten as plain tasks and show once more.

Highlight a sim's family now has two levels, picked on its banner: Close (partners, parents, children, siblings) and Extended, which adds grandparents, grandchildren, aunts and uncles, first cousins and step-family. Your choice is remembered.
Toolbar tooltips are short again and fit their box, with no empty space beside the text.
Select a link and click or tap a name on its label to jump to that sim's card.
The family links button's arrow now sits beside its icon instead of being squeezed into the corner, so it reads clearly as a menu.
Long toolbar tooltips now wrap inside their box instead of running out past it.

The Load .json dialog is clearer: first choose which sims and links end up on the board (add the file, or replace the board with it), then where the cards go. It says what Replace removes, and the button names what will happen.
Long file names now wrap in the Load .json and Load .save dialogs instead of making them scroll sideways.
New Organise button: it lays the whole board out like the starter one, with worlds in columns by how many households and sims they have and each household packed tight. Undo puts everything back.

A household whose parents live elsewhere no longer leaves an empty row above itself, which let the household under it overlap and pushed worlds into each other. Boards you already have stay exactly where they are; Organise uses the tighter packing.

The family links button now opens a menu: show all links, only those inside households (the lines between households hide), or none. Highlight a sim's family lights up whoever you select (partners, parents, children, siblings) and counts them and the households they live in.

Load .json now always asks how the file meets the board, even over the built-in starter board, so you can choose whose card positions win. On the starter board it picks Replace for you, since merging would bring back the premade sims your file leaves out.

Scrolling now moves the board: two fingers on a trackpad, or the mouse wheel. To zoom, pinch, or hold ⌘/Ctrl while you scroll. You can also pan in every mode: drag empty board in Connect to reach a far-off sim, or hold Space (or the middle mouse button) and drag anywhere, Select included. A Getting around card shows this once; Quick tips keeps it.
A + beside a household's Age up adds a new sim to it and opens their name, ready to type. In the sim editor, Enter now saves and closes.
Connect can now link secret lovers, a secret parent or secret child, and co-parents: two sims who aren't a couple but had a child together. Pick Co-parents, then click the child.
The tile grid now stays on screen while you pan, zoom or drag, instead of vanishing until you let go, so you can line cards up on the tiles they snap to.

Zoomed out, a world's name tag now grows up into the gap above its frame instead of down over the first household's tag, so every household's name stays readable and grabbable. Nothing on your board moves.

A relative your save keeps nameless now takes the starter roster's name when the family matches: Unknown Luna becomes Colin Sullivan, Eleanor's late son. Merge your save to rename the card; nothing moves.
13 starter sims now spell their names as the game does, like Chavez-Ralston, Eleanor Elderberry and Sofia Martinez, so a save matches them and fills in their details.
The sim editor now shows each sim's ID from your save, with a Copy ID button. Before you load a save, it tells you to.
Engaged couples from a save now get their link, labelled Engaged; the game's family tree leaves engagements out, so they had none. Merge your save to add them; nothing moves.

Ancestors from the game's family tree now come in with their real names, like Cordelia Thebe II or Cornelia Goth, instead of Unknown. Merge your save to rename the Unknown cards on your board; nothing moves, and any you renamed yourself keep your name.
Household name tags now fit their names, with even room on both sides; short names like Crumplebottom no longer run past the tag.
The tile grid no longer stops partway across a big board; it now fills the screen wherever you pan.

Horses from a save now come in as horses, not humans, and small dogs as dogs. Adopted children now get their adoptive parents, which the game's family tree leaves out. Merge your save to fix a board you already have; nothing moves.
Every sim card now has a ⠇ in its corner. Click it to edit the sim or move it to another household in one click, no double-click needed.

Filters now list every game. One your save doesn't have, like Journey to Batuu, stays listed and switched off instead of disappearing, and comes back on when its sims arrive. The load dialogs now fit the window: only their middle scrolls, so Proceed is always in reach.
You can now zoom out until the whole board fits the screen, past the old 6% limit. Age up only shows when you are close enough to read it, so a click far out no longer ages a household by accident.

Worlds now line up in columns: left to right by how many households they have, top to bottom by how many sims. Not in any world runs along the top, each household over the world its game brought, like Fia Acosta over Ondarion. Boards you already have open exactly as you left them.

Loading a save now adds the relatives the game's family tree keeps with no sim, as "Unknown" cards in their family, like Felix Hoffman's father between him and Bruno. Over the starter roster, Load save now picks Replace, so premades your game doesn't have stay out of your board.

Other is now Not in any world, as the game says. Premade sims with no home keep their own households there, like Bell and the Sotos; only sims the game made as you played share Unhoused sims. Merge your save to sort them; your board opens with every card where it was.
With the board open in two tabs, an older tab can no longer save over newer work from the other. It stops saving and shows a banner to reload, or to save its own version as a .json first.

Unhoused sims boxes now keep each family together, parents above children, and put sims with relatives elsewhere on the side facing them, so family lines no longer cross the box. A box you already have is rearranged in place; nothing else moves.

Unhoused sims (no home lot in the game) now share one "Unhoused sims" box per world, marked with a crossed-out house, instead of a box each. Merge your save to group them; those who only stood in a world when you saved move to Other.
Each world's tag now shows how many sims and households it has, like "👤 16 🏠 8". Hover a tag to see pets, deceased sims and anyone hidden by filters.
Sims who were out visiting when you saved no longer get a household box of their own. Merge your save again to bring them back to their family; everyone else stays where you put them.
Sim names and details now appear from 30% zoom instead of 35%.
Premade households from a save now show a readable name, like "Mysterious Rancher", instead of an internal game ID. Boards that already had them are renamed without moving any card.
Fix the Games filter being empty after replacing the board from a save: every sim now gets its game, and a hidden game always shows in the list so you can switch it back on.
Fix newer saves failing to import with "This save uses an index layout this reader does not handle". Saves from recent game versions load again.
On new boards, a household with a long name tag no longer covers the one beside it: the neighbour moves down to make room. Boards you already have keep every card exactly where it is.
When you load a file and keep your board positions, sims new to your board now fit in beside their family or world instead of landing on top of other households.
Importing a save no longer piles households and worlds on top of each other. Sims who join a family already on the board sit with that family, and anything below moves down to make room.
New Hide secrets filter: take secret lovers and secret parents off the board for spoiler-free screenshots. Nothing moves, and they come back when you turn it off.

Importing a save now shows secret lovers (a heart with a lock) and secret parents (a lock on the child's line), and tapping the line of parents who aren't a couple shows what they are to each other, like best friends.
Moving a sim on a big board is quicker: only the links near it are redrawn, not every link on the board.
Every child's line now reaches its parents. Lines no longer stop in mid-air when the parents aren't partners or when siblings sit to one side.
Big boards pan and zoom more smoothly: only the part around your view is drawn, and it keeps up as you move.
When you load a file and keep your board positions, your view stays where it was too.
Replace can now keep your board's positions, and merging a file brings its filters along. The dialog tells you first, and Undo puts yours back.
When you merge a JSON file, cards no longer jump around: they stay where they are, or go exactly where the file shows them.
Opening a filter panel now dims the board and moves the worlds list out of the way. Tap outside the panel to close it.
Quick tips is tidier and only opens when you ask for it, and filter panels slide up from the bottom on tablets and small laptops too.
Connect now refuses a link that would make a sim their own ancestor, and tells you why.
Fix the board freezing when two sims are linked as each other's parent.
Make big boards, like imported saves, rearrange about twice as fast after an edit.
Fix sims jumping back to where they started after you drag them.
When you merge a JSON file, you can now keep the card positions on this board or use the ones in the file.
Hide the changelog's own housekeeping entries.
Log the tooltip fix and the plain-language rewrite.
Rewrite this list in plain language, and drop the entries that only mean something to a programmer.
Stop the hover labels on the top bar running off the edge of the window.
Log the Developer updates panel in its own changelog.
Add this Developer updates list to the ⋮ menu, so you can see what has changed.
Worlds now stay where you drop them, including on top of each other.
Open the board faster by not drawing card names while you are zoomed too far out to read them.
Make the board appear sooner when you open the site.
Start counting which features get used, so the busiest ones get the most attention.
You can now click the shared line above a group of brothers and sisters, not only the branch down to each one.
Remove the Export PNG option from the ⋮ menu.
Keep relationship labels sitting on the line they describe, straighten family branches, and make saving and loading more reliable.
entries.compat: Saved files now record which version of the board made them. From here on, loading a file the board cannot lay out correctly tells you so and tidies it up, instead of quietly putting cards in the wrong places. Files saved before today have no such marker, so they always get re-arranged.

entries.text: Add importing a Sims 4 save file, add the little map in the corner, and stop worlds landing on top of each other.
entries.compat: Older .json files stop working properly here. This update moved every card onto a tile grid, so a board saved before today no longer lines up and will be re-arranged when you load it. Your sims, households and links all survive — only where you dragged things is lost.

entries.text: Your Filters choices are now saved with the board, so loading it back shows the same view.
Add gender to the sim editor, and pick one at random for new sims.
Reorganise the top bar so related buttons sit together and every filter shares one menu.
Add Age up for a whole household, add Undo, add Bloodline to dim everyone outside one family, and record all of it in the Log.
Add an infant straight from a couple, stop menus opening off the edge of the screen, and make the Log easier to read.
Add the Log of every link you make, and stop cards jumping about when you link sims or move a household.
Add a contact email to the ⋮ menu.
Correct the family links in the Other world against The Sims Wiki.
Make the board work properly on phones, with pinch to zoom and drag to pan, and drop new sims where you are looking.
Install Vercel Web Analytics.
Update repo and production URLs after GitHub rename.
Add the Credits panel, the project licence, and the Family Trees name.
Stop relationship lines running across cards they have nothing to do with.
Lay the Other world out in neat columns and keep related households side by side.
Arrange each household automatically, so parents sit above their children.
Stop the line to a child doubling back on itself when they sit just below their parents.
Collapse the header and toolbar into a single bar across the top.
Stop relationship lines taking long detours around cards.
Stop the board re-centring itself while you are dragging.
Make relationship lines meet cards from the side, so they are easier to follow.
Bring back the missing relationship symbols, and clear the line that stuck to the cursor after linking.
Fix the board not fitting the window when it opens, and tidy where the legend and the how-to note sit.
Fix the board not filling the whole window.
Fix Vercel build: pin Node 22 and configure pnpm install via corepack.
First version of the Family Trees Whiteboard.
